html:
An Algerian novelist, translator and filmmaker, born Fatima-Zohra Imalayen, who wrote in French about the lives of Algerian women under colonial rule and after.

The daughter of a teacher, she went to French schools in French Algeria and in 1955 became the first Algerian woman admitted to one of France's elite teacher training colleges. She took part in a student strike in support of the Algerian War of independence and published her first novel, La Soif, in 1957, under a pen name to spare her family.

Her best known books include Women of Algiers in Their Apartment (1980), named after a painting by Eugène Delacroix, and Fantasia: An Algerian Cavalcade (1985), which sets women's memories of the war against French records of the conquest of the 1830s. Her film The Nouba of the Women of Mount Chenoua (1977) won a prize at the Venice festival.

She taught in Algiers, Paris and New York. In 2005 she was elected to the Académie française, the first writer from the Maghreb to join it.
